html:
Ranavalona I was queen of Madagascar from 1828 to 1861, who resisted European influence and persecuted Malagasy Christians.

Widow of Radama I, she came to power with the backing of officials and keepers of the royal charms who feared foreign ideas. In 1835 she banned Christianity, and many believers were killed. Foreign missionaries left, and a French and British attack on the port of Tamatave in 1845 was beaten off.

She ruled harshly, with heavy forced labour and wars that cost many lives. Yet the Frenchman Jean Laborde built an industrial complex for her, making guns and goods. Her policy kept the kingdom independent. Her successors reopened the country, and Ranavalona II made the court Protestant in 1869. Her palace stood in the Rova of Antananarivo.
sum: Ranavalona I was queen of Madagascar from 1828 to 1861, who resisted European influence and persecuted Malagasy Christians.
